title: DORA's software delivery performance metrics
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Last updated 5 January 2026. Throughput: change lead time, deployment frequency, failed deployment recovery time; instability: change fail rate, deployment rework rate; warns against turning the metrics into targets and comparing unlike applications.

title: Postmortem Culture: Learning from Failure (Site Reliability Engineering, chapter 15)
publisher: Google SRE (John Lunney and Sue Lueder)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Postmortem triggers (user-visible downtime, data loss, on-call intervention such as rollback, long resolution, monitoring failure) set in advance; blameless focus on contributing causes; senior review; shared repository.

title: Managing Incidents (Site Reliability Engineering, chapter 14)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Roles: incident command, operations, communication, planning; only the ops team changes the system; a live incident state document; explicit handoff; declare an incident if a second team is needed, customers can see it, or it is unsolved after an hour of focused analysis.

title: Keep a Changelog 1.1.0
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Changelogs are for people; latest version first with dates; Unreleased section; Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security; commit logs are not changelogs; yanked releases marked [YANKED].

title: BlueGreenDeployment
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 1 March 2010, updated 5 June 2015. Two production environments, switch traffic, switch back to roll back; ship a backward-compatible schema change before the application change.

title: CanaryRelease
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 25 June 2014. Release to a small subset of users first, widen as confidence grows, route users back to the old version if problems appear.

title: Feature Toggles (aka Feature Flags)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 9 October 2017. Release, experiment, ops and permissioning toggles; ops toggles include long-lived kill switches; toggles carry a cost, so add removal tasks and expiry dates.

title: Building best practices
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Multi-stage builds; trusted minimal base images; tags are mutable, pin to a digest and update pins through reviewed pull requests; rebuild with --pull and --no-cache; .dockerignore; run as a non-root USER; combine apt-get update and install.

title: Docker Hub usage and limits
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Pull limits per 6 hours: unauthenticated 100 per IPv4 address or IPv6 /64; Personal (signed in, free) 200; paid plans unlimited, with fair-use limits.

title: Secure use reference (GitHub Actions)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Pin actions to a full-length commit SHA from the action's own repository, or use a workflow dependency lockfile; least GITHUB_TOKEN permissions; no structured data as secrets; rotate leaked secrets; pass untrusted input through environment variables; avoid pull_request_target with untrusted code; self-hosted runners almost never for public repos; OIDC instead of long-lived cloud keys.

title: Managing environments for deployment
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Up to 6 required reviewers, one approval needed, prevent self-review, wait timer, deployment branch and tag rules; environment secrets released only after protection rules pass; GitHub Free can configure environments only for public repositories.

title: Supply Chain Compromise of Third-Party tj-actions/changed-files (CVE-2025-30066) and reviewdog/action-setup@v1 (CVE-2025-30154)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Alert of 18 March 2025, revised 26 March 2025. Compromised action exposed secrets in workflow logs between 12 and 15 March 2025 (UTC); fixed in v46.0.1; CISA advised finding affected repos, treating exposed secrets as compromised and rotating them.

title: The lifecycle meta-argument
supports: Opened with WebFetch. prevent_destroy rejects plans that would destroy the resource but does not protect it if the resource block is removed; create_before_destroy; ignore_changes; replace_triggered_by.

title: terraform plan command reference
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Plan proposes changes without making them; -out saves a plan to apply exactly, and the file can contain sensitive values; -destroy and -refresh-only modes; -detailed-exitcode returns 0 no changes, 1 error, 2 changes present.

title: OpenTofu
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Open-source fork of Terraform under Linux Foundation stewardship, described as a drop-in replacement; 1.13 is the newest stable line; client-side state encryption since 1.7.

title: Managing your costs with AWS Budgets
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Cost, usage, RI and Savings Plans budgets; actual and forecast alerts; actions such as applying an IAM policy that denies new resources; data updated up to three times a day, 8 to 12 hours apart; costs can pass the threshold before the alert arrives.

title: Organizing and tracking costs using AWS cost allocation tags
supports: Opened with WebFetch. AWS-generated and user-defined tags must each be activated before they appear in Cost Explorer; tags can take up to 24 hours to appear; don't put sensitive information in tags; only the management account manages cost allocation tags.

title: Detecting unusual spend with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Machine learning on net unblended cost, runs about three times a day; up to 24 hours to detect an anomaly; new monitors take 24 hours; a new service needs 10 days of history; root causes by service, account, Region and usage type.

title: Create, edit, or delete budgets and budget alerts
supports: Opened with WebFetch (cloud.google.com redirects here). An alerts-only budget does not cap usage or spending; costs are reported with a delay; Pub/Sub notifications can automate controls such as disabling billing on a project; spend cap budgets exist for some services.

title: Tutorial: Create and manage budgets (Microsoft Cost Management)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Budgets alert but resources are not affected and consumption is not stopped; cost data typically available within 8 to 24 hours and budgets evaluated every 24 hours; up to five thresholds; action groups can trigger automation.

title: Restore testing (AWS Backup)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Scheduled restore tests of recovery points with restore time monitoring; restored resources deleted after an optional validation window; a cost per restore test; a separate account recommended for tests.

title: Falcon Content Update Preliminary Post Incident Report
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Content update released 04:09 UTC and reverted 05:27 UTC on 19 July 2024; Windows hosts on sensor 7.11+ crashed; a content validator bug let a faulty template through; fixes include staggered canary deployment and customer control over update timing.

title: Helping our customers through the CrowdStrike outage
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 20 July 2024: Microsoft estimated the update affected 8.5 million Windows devices, less than one percent of all Windows machines.

title: Summary of the Amazon DynamoDB Service Disruption in the Northern Virginia (US-EAST-1) Region
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 19 October 2025, 11:48 PM PDT to 20 October 2025, 2:20 PM PDT; a latent race condition in DynamoDB's DNS automation left an empty DNS record; knock-on failures in EC2 launches, Network Load Balancer, Lambda, ECS, EKS, Fargate, STS and IAM sign-in; AWS disabled the automation worldwide pending fixes.

title: Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Failures from 11:20 UTC, core traffic largely restored by 14:30, all systems normal at 17:06 UTC; a database permissions change doubled a generated Bot Management feature file past a 200-feature limit; not an attack; fixes include treating generated config like user input and more global kill switches.

title: SEC Adopts Rules on Cybersecurity Risk Management, Strategy, Governance, and Incident Disclosure by Public Companies (2023-139)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Public companies disclose material cybersecurity incidents under Form 8-K Item 1.05, generally within four business days of deciding the incident is material; delay possible on national security or public safety grounds.

title: NIS2 Directive: securing network and information systems
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Member states had until 17 October 2024 to transpose NIS2; medium-sized and large entities in 18 critical sectors take risk-management measures and notify national authorities of significant incidents. The page gives no reporting deadlines.

title: NIS Directive and NIS Regulations 2018
supports: Opened with WebFetch. UK NIS Regulations in force 10 May 2018; cover essential services and digital services including online marketplaces, online search engines and cloud computing services; updates planned, including incident reporting; links a Cyber Security and Resilience Bill collection.

title: Release a version update in phases
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 7-day phased release (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100%) for automatic updates; manual updates always possible; pause up to 30 days in total; release to all at any time.

title: Release app updates with staged rollouts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Percentage rises only when you raise it; halting stops new users getting the version but people who have it keep it; resume only if the bundle is fine; updates only.
